messages:
julia: Quick sync — we need to pick a practical transport strategy for internal model routing + quotas + telemetry. TL;DR: proto-first gRPC gives typed contracts and smaller payloads, but client onboarding friction; gateway/transcoding gives REST ergonomics but extra moving parts. I'm leaning towards a small proto-first pilot and a lightweight gateway for browser clients. Thoughts?

mike: +1 to a pilot. My worry is double-work for infra if we keep both long-term. typed contracts cut runtime errors though.

anya: From console/telemetry POV we care about stable route identifiers and consistent header propagation. Gateway can obscure upstream route names unless we pass x-internal-route. If we do proto-first, make sure we have a mapping layer that preserves route tags for metrics.

sam: Quotas: enforcement at the edge (gateway) is easiest for blowouts, but per-model token accounting lives downstream. If we do gateway + grpc backend we need a reliable way to annotate requests with token-estimates before enforcement. Otherwise we get misattributed usage.

mike: Agreed. Options: 1) gateway enforces a conservative per-request token cap using an estimate header; 2) gateway proxies but defers enforcement to a quota-service that the runtime calls back to after generation. Both have pros/cons (latency vs accuracy).

anya: For rollout UX, we should support canaries by tenant and by route weight. Console should show live delta in latency/cost/quality for canaries. If we adopt proto-first, we can add a version header (x-model-api-v) so rollouts are visible in telemetry.

julia: Note: we also want tracing to connect client request -> gateway -> runtime -> quota decisions -> model shard. That implies consistent request IDs and sampled spans. Prefer not to add another mapping layer that breaks span continuity.

kevin: small nit — browser clients often just want simple fetch JSON. Running a gateway that translates to grpc is trivial for us. But do not ignore server-to-server callers; typed clients reduce bugs.

sam: Practical experiment idea: pick 3 endpoints (embeddings, chat, rerank) and implement proto-first on backend; add a thin JSON gateway for browser SDKs. Run both for 2 weeks on staging, collect: P95 latency, median cost/tokens, error rates, telemetry completeness (span continuity, route labels), quota misattribution events.

mike: Also measure dev velocity: time to implement client for a new language. That’s where proto-first might lose for product teams.

anya: Console changes we need for the pilot: allow filtering by x-model-api-v header, show per-version breakdown, and a small canary bake-in dashboard. I can sketch a mock in 2 days.

julia: Sounds good. Decision: greenlight pilot. Action items: julia-> create RFC doc with API examples; mike-> prototype proto defs and runtime adapter; anya-> mock console panels; sam-> quota enforcement experiment plan.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: experiment/proto-pilot has been deployed to staging (commit abc123) — monitors live. :rocket:

mike: One more implementation detail — keep backward-compatible JSON examples in proto annotations so we can autogenerate gateway mappings. That should reduce manual glue.

julia: Agreed. Let's keep the migration path simple for teams: autogen clients + gateway for browsers. We can iterate on whether to standardize on proto-first long-term after pilot metrics.

anya: I'll add required telemetry tags to the mock: route_id, model_variant, api_version, tenant_id, request_estimated_tokens. Example header snippet to standardize:

```
X-Internal-Route: models.chat.generate
X-Model-Api-Version: v2
X-Estimated-Tokens: 42
```

sam: Perfect. For quota enforcement experiment I'll try both conservative gateway-enforced caps and deferred quota-check to see which causes less user-visible failures.

julia: Thanks everyone. I'll open the RFC and link the pilot checklist here. If you have objections speak up today, otherwise we'll start tomorrow. :+1:

kevin: no objections from my side. excited to see the telemetry side-by-side.

ops-bot: alert-bot: smoke tests passed for staging/proto-pilot (all checks green).
